questions.text: If a RUN would produce more results than the output FIFO has room for, because earlier outputs have not been drained, should RUN stall until space is free, drop the surplus outputs, process only as many samples as fit, or be refused? Must SAMPLES_DONE, SAT_COUNT and the filter history still include the samples whose outputs were lost?
questions.answer: The run processes only as many samples as there is room for in the output FIFO and leaves the rest in the input FIFO. It does not stall, drop outputs, or refuse the run. Because no outputs are lost, the question about counting samples whose outputs were lost does not arise. SAMPLES_DONE counts only the samples actually processed.
questions.evidence: - The output FIFO has 1,024 words. If a run would produce more outputs than there is room in the output FIFO, the run processes only as many samples as there is room for and leaves the rest in the input FIFO; SAMPLES_DONE counts what was processed. Nothing is dropped or overwritten.

questions.text: Does SCRATCH read 0? (Scenario: SCRATCH is written 0xCAFEF00D, then rst is asserted by power-up sequence again (8 clk_25 cycles), then SCRATCH is read.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes. SCRATCH resets to 0, so after rst is asserted again the read returns 0, not 0xCAFEF00D.
questions.evidence: | 0x008 | SCRATCH | RW | 32 bits, reads back what was written, resets to 0 |

questions.text: What is the input FIFO count after both writes take effect? (Scenario: In the same clk_25 cycle, h_we writes CLEAR via CTRL and another interface cycle is not possible, so IN_PUSH is written in the next cycle (h_we on consecutive cycles: CLEAR then IN_PUSH 0x0042).) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: 1. The CLEAR write takes effect one clock after its h_we and empties the FIFOs. The IN_PUSH write comes one cycle later and takes effect one clock after its own h_we, so it lands after the clear. The FIFO is not full, so the sample 0x0042 is accepted and the input FIFO count is 1.
questions.evidence: A write takes effect the clock after `h_we`.

questions.text: What does STATUS bits 15:4 read afterwards, as a decimal count? (Note 1024 does not fit in 12 bits... state the value read) (Scenario: Input FIFO holds 1,024 samples. The host writes IN_PUSH with 0x1234 again while RUN is not active.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: STATUS bits 15:4 still read 1024. The push is ignored because the input FIFO is full, so the count does not change. 1024 does fit in the 12-bit field (it holds up to 4095), so the note in the question does not apply. In the STATUS register the field is 0x400 at bits 15:4, which makes the register's low half 0x4000 while BUSY is 0.
questions.evidence: IN_PUSH with a full input FIFO is ignored; the sample is lost and not counted.

questions.text: How many entries are popped in total and what is the final-cycle read value (give number of entries popped)? (Scenario: Output FIFO holds exactly 1 entry 0x0005. h_re is held high for 3 consecutive clk_25 cycles on OUT_POP.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?

questions.text: What is SAT_COUNT after the run? (Does an output exactly equal to 32767 count as saturated?) (Scenario: One RUN produces three outputs whose pre-clamp values are 40000, -40000 and 32767, starting after CLEAR.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: SAT_COUNT is 2. The outputs 40000 and -40000 are clipped to +32767 and -32768, so each counts once. The output 32767 is already inside the 16-bit signed range, so nothing is clipped and it does not count.
questions.evidence: Saturation clips to -32768 and +32767 and increments SAT_COUNT once per saturated output; SAT_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps.

questions.text: Is BUSY (bit 0) 0, and what happens to the 500 unprocessed input samples and the already produced outputs: are the FIFO counts both 0? (Scenario: RUN is in progress with 500 of 1000 input samples processed when rst asserts. After rst deasserts the host reads STATUS.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. After reset BUSY is 0 and both FIFO counts are 0. Reset empties both FIFOs, so the 500 unprocessed input samples and the outputs already produced are discarded. STATUS reads 0, the filter history is zero, and SAT_COUNT and SAMPLES_DONE are 0.
questions.evidence: - Reset: both FIFOs empty, the filter history zero, SAT_COUNT 0, SAMPLES_DONE 0, STATUS 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: How many entries are popped from the output FIFO? (Scenario: Output FIFO holds 3 entries A, B, C. Host holds h_re high for two consecutive clk_25 cycles at OUT_POP address.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
What happens to this push? (Scenario: RUN is in progress (BUSY=1) and the host writes IN_PUSH with 0x0001 while the input FIFO has room.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: The push is accepted because the input FIFO has room. If it arrives before the FIFO has been drained, it is processed in the same run; otherwise it is processed in the next run.
questions.evidence: IN_PUSH while BUSY is accepted if there is room and is processed in the same run if it arrives before the FIFO has been drained, else in the next run.

questions.text: What does sfp_tx_disable show, and does ID read 0x20940001? (Scenario: Immediately after power-up, during the 8-cycle rst hold before MMCM-locked reset completes, the host reads ID at 0x000.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: sfp_tx_disable (if the design drives it) is held at 1 (laser off) at all times, including during reset. The spec does not say whether ID at 0x000 must read 0x20940001 during the rst hold or before the MMCM locks, so that part is not specified. It only says the ID register reads 0x20940001 and is read-only.
questions.evidence: `sfp_tx_disable` pin, it holds it at 1 (laser off) at all times, and it uses no GT transceiver channel, at most the GT reference clock buffer.

questions.answer: 76 samples remain. The output FIFO has room for 1,024 - 100 = 924 results, so the run processes 924 of the 1,000 samples and leaves the other 76 in the input FIFO. This assumes nothing is popped from the output FIFO during the run.
questions.evidence: The output FIFO has 1,024 words. If a run would produce more outputs than there is room in the output FIFO, the run processes only as many samples as there is room for and leaves the rest in the input FIFO; SAMPLES_DONE counts what was processed. Nothing is dropped or overwritten.

questions.text: What value is read in hex? (Scenario: The host writes 0x12345678 to unmapped address 0x7F0, then reads 0x7F0.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: 0x00000000. Unmapped addresses read 0 and ignore writes, so the write to 0x7F0 has no effect and the read returns 0.
questions.evidence: Unmapped addresses read 0 and ignore writes.
